baby-toddler-fruit-and-vegetables-stage-.title: Baby Toddler fruit and vegetables, Stage 3

content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler fruit and vegetables, Stage 3 is a ready‑to‑serve puree blend of fruits and vegetables designed for children aged 12–24 months. The purees are made from 100 % natural ingredients with no added sugar, salt or preservatives. Each pouch contains a child‑sized portion that is easy to feed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend contains only fresh, pesticide‑free fruits and vegetables.
The product meets strict European baby‑food safety standards.
Each serving is nutritionally balanced with carbohydrates, protein and healthy fats to support growth.
Packaging is made from food‑grade plastic that is microwave‑safe.
A variety of flavor combinations helps develop a child’s palate.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Fruits and vegetables provide vitamin B6 and folate, essential for normal nervous‑system development.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps establish a beneficial gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in sodium
items.content: No added salt makes the product gentle on a toddler’s kidneys.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients from berries and vegetables protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to individual ingredients
items.content: Introduce the product gradually and watch for reactions to specific fruits or vegetables.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Puree must be fully smooth with no large pieces, especially for children under 12 months.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Use opened pouches within 24 hours and keep them refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the puree in the microwave for 30‑40 seconds or in warm water. If needed, thin with a small amount of breast milk or formula to reach the desired consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened pouches in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep in the refrigerator and consume within one day.

content.title: About
content.content: Cuban bread is a traditional white loaf with a crisp crust and a soft, slightly airy crumb. It is made from simple flour, water, yeast, salt, and a touch of sugar. The dough is given a long fermentation, and before baking small holes are poked in it, giving the loaf its characteristic appearance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cuban bread is often called “pan de batata,” although the recipe contains no sweet potato; the name refers to the loaf’s shape resembling a batata.
Traditionally the bread is baked in open‑flame ovens, which impart a distinctive smoky aroma to the crust.
In Cuba the bread is a symbol of hospitality and is served at every meal.
In the 1990s the first bakeries specializing in Cuban bread opened in the United States, helping spread its popularity beyond the Caribbean.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Cuban bread provides a quick source of energy thanks to its high content of complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many other breads, Cuban bread contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: During fermentation, yeast produces B1, B2, and B3 vitamins that support normal metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The large pores in the crumb aid digestion and lead to a slower rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The bread contains gluten, so it should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because its carbohydrates are quickly absorbed, the bread can raise blood sugar levels, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Traditional recipes use a moderate amount of salt; it can be reduced if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cuban bread is perfect for sandwiches, serving alongside soups, salads, and roasted meats. It is often buttered or used as the base for the classic Cuban sandwich “Cubano” with ham, roasted pork, cheese, and pickles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, freeze it and reheat in the oven before serving.

carrots-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked-wit.title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots with reduced sodium are made from selected carrot roots that are blanched, then cooked in butter or margarine and sealed in airtight jars. The lower salt level makes the product suitable for low‑sodium diets, while the added fat enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots have been cultivated for over 5,000 years and are one of the oldest cultivated vegetables.
Canning preserves the nutritional value of carrots for 2–3 years when stored properly.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with natural herbs and spices.
Cooking in butter or margarine increases the bioavailability of beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
Carrots are rich in antioxidants such as lutein and zeaxanthin, which support eye health.

items.title: High in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted in the body to vitamin A, essential for vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and the reduced sodium content lessens strain on the heart.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect cells from oxidative stress, promoting healthy eyes.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 35 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to carrots, ranging from itching to swelling.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Because the product is cooked in butter or margarine, individuals monitoring saturated fat intake should account for this.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, the product still contains salt; those with severe hypertension should consider it in their daily limit.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten cold in salads, added to soups, stews, and side dishes, used as a sandwich filling, or incorporated into baby foods. They can also be gently warmed in a skillet with a little extra butter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if the jar bulges, leaks, or develops an off odor.

chicken-thigh-fried-coated-skin-coating-.title: Chicken thigh, fried, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh is the dark meat located on the upper part of the bird's leg. When fried in a coating it develops a crunchy crust, and the skin and coating remain edible. The product is prepared from raw meat (code 844) and is common in fast‑food dishes, snacks, and family meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken thighs contain more iron and zinc than breast meat because of their darker color.
Frying in a coating triggers the Maillard reaction, giving a characteristic aroma and golden hue.
Chicken skin is rich in collagen, which retains its structure when cooked properly.
Different cultures use various coatings, from breadcrumbs to cornflakes.
Thighs cook faster than breast meat thanks to higher fat content.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: It supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Dark meat offers more heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: The fat in thighs makes the dish more satiating and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: When eaten, the skin provides collagen beneficial for skin, joints, and connective tissue.

items.title: Higher fat intake
items.content: Thighs are fattier than breast meat, so portion control is advisable for calorie‑conscious individuals.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Pathogen risk
items.content: Raw chicken can harbor Salmonella and Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium in coating
items.content: Pre‑made breadings often contain salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried coated chicken thighs are great as a hot snack, added to salads, sandwiches, or served with dipping sauces. The skin and coating can be eaten together with the meat for extra crunch and flavor. Let the dish rest briefly after cooking to keep the crust crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw thighs in the refrigerator at +2–4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked pieces keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or in the freezer for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before eating.

cookie-with-peanut-butter-filling-chocol.title: Cookie with Peanut Butter Filling, Chocolate-Coated

content.title: About
content.content: A cookie with a peanut butter filling, coated in dark chocolate, is a crunchy dessert with a smooth nutty center and a sweet‑bitter chocolate shell. It is made from wheat flour, sugar, eggs, butter, peanut butter filling, and a chocolate glaze.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The peanut‑chocolate combination is a classic pairing widely used in confectionery.
The chocolate coating protects the filling from drying out and extends shelf life.
Peanut butter provides natural plant protein and healthy monounsaturated fats.
These cookies are often served as a small dessert with coffee or tea.
In some countries similar treats are called “chocolate‑covered peanut bars.”

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Peanut butter contains plant‑based protein that helps maintain muscle tissue.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats in peanuts may support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peanuts provide niacin, folate, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate is high in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and fats delivers quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with peanut allergy should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Sugar and fat make the cookie calorie‑dense, so portion size should be moderate.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oils are used, the product may contain trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie is convenient as a standalone snack, paired with coffee, tea, or milk. It can be broken into pieces for dessert salads, ice cream toppings, or as a garnish for cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate coating from melting. Keep moisture away to maintain the crisp texture.
